transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you so much for taking the time to see me. Um, I hope I'm in the right place. I guess I'm mostly here because of some... well, some stress at work. Is it okay if I just explain a little bit about what's been going on? 

I work as a transportation inspector, and, um, a little while ago I actually got this county safety award. Which was really nice, you know? I was proud of it. But... well, ever since then, I've been noticing that certain people at work are kind of twisting my inspection reports. They keep asking these really pointed budget questions, too. I don't want to sound difficult or, you know, complain too much, but it really feels like they're trying to make me look crooked. 

I even brought it up to my supervisor, and he said it's just a normal review process, but... I don't know, I can just tell there's a coordinated effort to discredit me. I'm sorry if that sounds strange or if I'm not explaining it right... I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information. Does that make sense?
Do you think these people at work are targeting you specifically?

Um... yeah. I do. I really hope I don't sound, you know, paranoid or anything by saying that. I always try to be a good team player, I really do. But... yes, it feels like it's just me they're focusing on. 

Like I was saying, it all started right after that county safety award. It's like certain people are taking *my* specific inspection reports and twisting them around. And the budget questions they keep asking me, they're just so pointed... it really feels like they're trying to set me up to look crooked. I want to believe my supervisor when he says it's just a normal review process, I really try to listen to him, but... I can just tell there's this coordinated effort to discredit me. 

I know how all of that sounds, and I'm sorry if it seems like I'm overreacting or being difficult. I just... I can't shake the feeling. Do you think I'm making too big a deal out of this?
Do you think these people at work would be doing this to you even if you weren't a transportation inspector?

Oh, um... wow, I actually haven't really thought about it like that before. I'm... I'm not really sure, to be honest. 

I mean, the reports and the safety award, they're all tied to my job as an inspector, so... I guess I just always assumed it was because of the work I'm doing right now. If I was in a totally different department or, you know, not an inspector at all... I don't know if they'd still be doing this. I really hope they wouldn't. I always try to get along with everyone and be well-liked, no matter what my role is. 

I'm sorry, I wish I had a better answer for you on that one. Does that... does that make sense, or did you need me to think about it a different way? I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need.
Do you think these people at work are actually out to get you, or is it just their actions that make you feel that way?

Um... I really want to say it's just my feelings. I know that would probably be the, um, the better answer, and I really don't want to come across like I'm accusing people unjustly or being difficult. I try so hard to give everyone the benefit of the doubt and just do a good job. 

But... well, I really do think they're actually trying to make me look crooked. Like I mentioned before, it's the actual things they are doing—the way they're twisting my inspection reports and bringing up those pointed budget questions. It's just too specific to be an accident. I really wish I could just agree with my supervisor when he says it's just a normal review, because that would be so much easier, right? I want to believe him. But deep down, I can just tell there’s a coordinated effort to discredit me. 

I'm sorry, I know saying they are out to get me sounds so extreme, and I really hate sounding like that. I hope I'm not coming off as unreasonable or, you know, paranoid... is it okay that I'm explaining it this way? I just want to be as honest with you as I can.
How long have you been feeling like these people at work are trying to discredit you?

Um... well, it's been a little while now. I really hope it doesn't make me sound, you know, obsessive or anything for letting it bother me for this long. But... I guess it's been going on for about a year now. 

Yeah, right around a year. Like I was saying earlier, it really seemed to start right after I got recognized for that county safety initiative. Everything was totally fine before that, I promise. I got along with everyone. I actually tried to just ignore it for the longest time because I really just want to keep the peace and be a good employee, you know? I kept telling myself it would blow over. 

Does... does that timeline make sense to you? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information. I hope I'm explaining things okay.
Do you feel like people are trying to discredit you or harm you outside of work as well?

Oh, no, no, definitely not. It's really just at work. 

I mean, I have a pretty quiet life outside of the office. I go to the grocery store, I run my errands, and people are perfectly nice to me. I've never felt like anyone at the store or, you know, my neighbors or anyone like that are treating me any differently or trying to cause me trouble. I really try to be a good neighbor and just be polite to everyone I meet. 

So, yeah, it's strictly just the people in my department who are involved in all of this. I really hope that makes me sound a bit more grounded? Like, I know how it sounds when I talk about the office, but I promise I'm not walking around thinking everyone in the world is against me. I really just want things to be normal. Is that... is that helpful to know?
Do you feel like these people at work are trying to discredit you as a person, or is it just about your work performance?

Um... I think it's mostly about my work performance. I really don't think they have anything against me personally, you know? Like, as a person. 

I try to be a good guy. I always say good morning, I bring donuts sometimes... I really try to be pleasant to work with. So I don't think they hate *me*. It's just... it's about the job. They just want to make it look like I'm not doing my job right, or that I'm cutting corners on my inspections. 

I really hope that makes sense. I don't want to sound like I think I'm so important that they're just obsessed with ruining my whole life or anything. It's really just about the work stuff, and getting me out of the way there. Does that sound... I don't know, a little more reasonable? I just want to make sure I'm answering you the right way.
Do you think your belief that they are trying to discredit you could be mistaken?

Um... well, I mean, I guess anyone can be mistaken about things sometimes, right? I try to be open-minded, I really do. But... I don't know, it's just so hard to ignore what's right in front of me. 

Like I was saying, it all started after that county safety award. Ever since then, it's just been... well, certain people at work, they take my inspection reports and they kind of twist them around. And then they started asking all these really pointed questions about the budget, almost like they're trying to make me look crooked or something. 

I've even talked to my supervisor about it, because I really want to do a good job and make sure everything is okay. But he just tells me it's normal review stuff. But... I don't know, I can just tell. I can feel it. It really feels like there's this coordinated effort to discredit me. 

I really hope I don't sound crazy saying that. I know it sounds a little intense, but I'm just trying to be honest with you about what's happening. Do you... do you think it's possible I'm just misreading it? I mean, I'm pretty sure about what they're doing, but I really value your opinion on it. I just want to make sure I'm looking at this the right way.
Do you think there's any possibility that you're misinterpreting the actions of your coworkers?

I mean... I'd really like to think I am. I don't want to be stubborn about this, I promise. I know I just mentioned the whole thing with the safety award, and how they've been twisting my inspection reports... and I know my supervisor says it's just a normal review process. I really try to listen to him, because I want to be a good employee and take feedback well. 

But... I don't know, when they keep asking those really pointed budget questions, almost like they're actively trying to make me look crooked... it's just really hard to see it as a simple misunderstanding. Even if I really wish it was just me misinterpreting things, it just feels so clearly like a coordinated effort to discredit me. 

I'm sorry if that's not the answer you were hoping for, or if it makes me sound difficult. I'm really trying to look at it from all sides, I just... I don't see how else to explain what they're doing. Is it okay that I feel that way? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Do you think your coworkers' actions are part of a larger plot against you?

Oh, um... no, no, I don't think it's anything like that. A larger plot? No, I really don't think so. 

I mean, I'm just a transportation inspector, you know? I'm not... I'm not anyone important enough for some big, massive conspiracy or anything. I don't think there's some huge shadowy group out to get me. It's really just those few specific people at the office who are upset about the award and want my job. 

I really try to keep things in perspective. I don't want you to think I'm sitting at home coming up with wild theories about the whole world being against me, because I'm really not. It's just a workplace thing. Just a few disgruntled coworkers trying to push me out. 

Does that... does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it okay. I just want to be sure you know I'm looking at this realistically, just dealing with an office politics issue, not... not anything bigger than that. Is that a helpful answer?
Do you think your belief that coworkers are trying to discredit you is based on facts or just a feeling?

Um... well, I really hope it's based on facts. I mean, I try to be a very logical person, you know? I don't want to be someone who just goes off of feelings or gets overly emotional about things at work. 

I know I've mentioned it a few times already, so I'm sorry if I'm repeating myself, but... the things they're doing, like twisting my inspection reports and asking those really pointed budget questions... to me, those are actual things happening. They're real actions. It's not just a vague feeling I have. It all started right after that county safety award, and I can literally see how they're treating my work differently now, almost like they're trying to make me look crooked. 

I know my supervisor says it's just normal review, and I really, really try to take his word for it because I respect him. But when I look at the actual facts of how my reports are being handled... I can just tell there's a coordinated effort to discredit me. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound unreasonable. I really try to base my thoughts on what's actually happening in front of me, not just my imagination. Do you think that's a fair way for me to look at it? I just want to make sure I'm making sense to you.
Do you think it's possible that your coworkers are not actually trying to discredit you, and you're just misunderstanding their actions?

I mean... I really, really want to say yes. I want to be the kind of person who can just admit they're wrong and move on. I don't want to be difficult or... or cause trouble, you know? 

But... it's just so hard to ignore what's right in front of me. Like I said, ever since I got that county safety award, the way they've been twisting my inspection reports... and the way they keep asking those really pointed budget questions... it really feels like they're trying to make me look crooked. 

I know my supervisor says it's just a normal review, and I really do want to believe him. I want to be a team player. But when I look at how everything is happening, I just... I can tell there's a coordinated effort to discredit me. I've tried so hard to see it as a misunderstanding, I promise I have. 

I'm sorry, I know I sound like a broken record. I'm probably not giving you the answer you want to hear, and I really hate that. I just... I don't want to lie to you. Is it okay that I still feel this way? I'm really trying my best to be objective, I just can't shake it.
Have you ever had a period of time where you didn't feel like your coworkers were trying to discredit you?

Oh, um... yes, absolutely. I mean, before all this started, everything was fine. We all got along really well, or at least I thought we did. I never had any issues with anyone. 

It really just... it started about a year ago. That's when everything shifted. It was right after I got recognized for that county safety initiative. Before that, I never felt like anyone was watching me or questioning my work. But for the last year, it's just been this constant... pressure, I guess? 

I really wish things could go back to how they were before the award. I don't like feeling this way, and I don't want to be someone who holds onto grudges for a whole year. I hope you don't think I'm just dwelling on the past. I really do try to come in every day with a fresh start, but it's just been going on for so long now. Does that make sense? I hope that answers your question okay.
Do you think your coworkers' behavior towards you is based on something you've done or something about you personally?

Um... well... I guess I've thought about that a lot. I really try to reflect on my own actions, you know? I want to make sure I'm doing a good job and being a good person to work with. 

I don't... I don't *think* I've done anything wrong. I mean, I won that safety award, which was supposed to be a good thing, right? I worked really hard on that initiative. But sometimes I wonder if... maybe I shouldn't have accepted it? Or maybe I seemed too proud of it? I really hope I didn't come across as arrogant or anything. I try to be very humble. 

As for something about me personally... I don't know. I try to be friendly and helpful to everyone. I really do. But maybe there's something about me that just rubs them the wrong way? I'd hate to think that's the case. I just want to do my inspections and keep everyone safe. 

I'm sorry, I don't know if that's a very good answer. I just... I don't want to blame them entirely if maybe I did something to upset them without realizing it. Does that seem like a reasonable way to look at it? I just want to make sure I'm being fair.
Have your feelings about your coworkers trying to discredit you changed at all over the past year?

I... well, I really wish I could tell you that they've faded, or that I've gotten over it. I know that's probably what you're hoping to hear, and I really hate to disappoint you... 

But honestly... no, they haven't really changed. I know I'm kind of repeating myself, and I'm sorry for that, but it's just been this steady thing ever since the safety award. The way they twist those inspection reports, and those budget questions... it still just feels exactly like they're trying to make me look crooked. 

My supervisor still tells me it's just a normal review, and I always nod and agree with him because I want to be cooperative. I really don't want to be a problem employee. But deep down... I can still tell it's a coordinated effort to discredit me. It hasn't stopped or gotten any better. 

I'm sorry, I know I probably sound so stubborn. Am I being too difficult by feeling this way? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the honest truth, even if it's not the best answer.
Do you think your belief that coworkers are trying to discredit you would change if you were presented with evidence that disproved it?

Oh, um... I would really like to say yes. I know that's probably the right answer, and I really want to be open-minded for you. I try so hard to be reasonable and cooperative... 

But... if I'm being completely honest, and I hope it's okay to say this... it would be really, really hard to just change my mind. I promise I would look at whatever evidence you showed me! I would. But it's just... ever since that county safety award, I've seen firsthand how they twist my inspection reports. And they keep asking those really pointed budget questions, just... trying to make me look crooked. 

Even when my supervisor talks to me and says it's just a normal review, and I smile and agree with him because I really want to be a good employee... I can still just tell there's a coordinated effort to discredit me. It's all so connected. So if someone handed me proof that nothing was going on, I think I'd just worry that the proof was faked or manipulated as part of the whole thing. 

I'm so sorry, I know that probably makes me sound incredibly stubborn, and I really hate that. I don't want to be a difficult person. Does it make sense why it would be hard for me to just accept a piece of paper saying everything is fine? I hope I'm not frustrating you with my answer.
Do you think it's possible that your perception of your coworkers' actions is not based in reality?

I... gosh, I really want to give you the answer you're looking for. I know that sometimes people get stressed and imagine things, and I really try to be self-aware about that. I always want to be a reasonable person, you know? I don't want to be one of those people who just makes up problems out of thin air.

But... I just don't see how it could be my imagination. I really don't. I'm sorry if that's not what you want to hear. It's just... the things they're doing are so specific. Like I said, the way they twist the details in my inspection reports, and the way they ask those budget questions... it's all designed to make me look crooked, ever since I got that county safety award. 

I know my supervisor says it's just a normal review, and I swear to you, I always tell him I understand, because I want to be a good team player. I really do. But I can just tell, deep down, that there's a coordinated effort to discredit me. It feels very, very real to me. 

I'm sorry, I know I'm probably coming across as really defensive, and I don't mean to be. I just... I can't imagine that I'm making all of this up. Does that make me sound completely unreasonable? I just want to be honest with you about what I'm experiencing.

Do you think your belief that coworkers are trying to discredit you would change if everyone at work, including your supervisor, told you that it's not true and that they're actually happy with your performance?

I... oh, wow. That would be really nice to hear. I mean, I'd love it if everyone just came out and said they were happy with my work. I really want to be liked, and I want to do a good job for them. I know I keep saying that, and I hope you believe me. 

But... if they all got together and told me that... I think I'd just wonder why they were suddenly doing it. Like, why now, you know? Because... well, I know I've told you this, but ever since that county safety award, the things they do with my inspection reports... they really twist the details. And the budget questions they ask me are just so pointed. It really feels like they're trying to make me look crooked. 

So if my supervisor and everyone else suddenly told me everything was fine... I'd probably still smile and thank them, because I don't want to rock the boat or be difficult. I'd act like I believed it. But inside... I think I'd just feel like it was another part of the coordinated effort to discredit me. Like maybe they were just trying to get me to let my guard down. 

I'm so sorry, I know that sounds terrible, like I can't trust anyone. I really don't want to be a paranoid person, and I hate that I can't just take a compliment. Am I being too difficult by saying that? I just... I want to make sure I'm giving you the right answer, even if it's not a very nice one.
Do you think your belief that coworkers are trying to discredit you would change if you were presented with undeniable proof that it's not true?

Oh, um... I feel like I'm probably giving you the exact same answer again, and I'm really sorry if I'm being repetitive. I promise I'm trying to be helpful and answer everything the right way for you. 

If someone gave me truly undeniable proof... I would really, really want to accept it. I'd probably just nod and say thank you, because I always try to be cooperative and I don't want to be a difficult person. But... inside? I think I'd still struggle. 

Because, like I was saying before, it's just been so clear ever since I got that county safety award. I see exactly how they twist my inspection reports, and they keep asking me those pointed budget questions just to make me look crooked. And even when my supervisor sits me down and tells me it's just a normal review... I can still just tell there's a coordinated effort to discredit me. 

So even if the proof looked undeniable, I think I'd just worry that they manufactured it to trick me. I know that sounds terrible, and I really wish I could just give you a simple yes. I hope I'm not disappointing you with these answers. Am I doing okay explaining all this?
Do you think you would ever be able to completely trust your coworkers again?

I... gosh, I really want to say yes. I would love to just go back to how things were and trust everyone completely. I always try to be friendly and professional, I promise I do. 

But... honestly? It's been a little hard to do that lately. I guess... well, the biggest consequence of all this is that things like our compliance reviews, or even just when I'm supposed to be mentoring the younger inspectors... it's all just gotten a little tense. I try to hide it, I really do, because I want to be a good mentor and a good team player. But I have found myself sort of... pulling back from a few coworkers I really used to trust. 

I just keep to myself a bit more now so I don't cause any problems or make anyone uncomfortable. Does that make sense? I hope I don't sound like I'm just being bitter or holding a grudge. I really just want to do my job well and make sure I'm giving you the honest answer, even if it's not the best one.
